name: MonarchIssueCard
title: IssueCard
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.Surface drawn as MonarchCard, androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow; MonarchStatusPicker and MonarchPriorityPicker (androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenu), MonarchTag, MonarchAvatar
summary: An issue on a board or in a list: key, title, status, priority, tags, due date and assignee, with status and priority changeable in place.
whenToUse: For issues, tasks or tickets in a board column or a list, where readers scan status, urgency, ownership and dates and open the issue from the title.
whenNotToUse: For a dense list with many columns, use a list of rows with a detail screen. For a calendar entry, use MonarchEventChip. For a plain card without issue fields, use MonarchCard.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchIssueCard(title: String, key: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, status: MonarchStatusOption? = null, statuses: List<MonarchStatusOption> = emptyList(), priority: MonarchPriorityLevel? = null, assignee: MonarchIssueCardAssignee? = null, tags: List<String> = emptyList(), dueDate: Long? = null, today: Long? = null, selected: Boolean = false, dragging: Boolean = false, labels: MonarchIssueCardLabels = MonarchIssueCardLabels(), onStatusChange: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, onPriorityChange: ((MonarchPriorityLevel) -> Unit)? = null, onOpen: (() -> Unit)? = null)
sealed interface MonarchIssueCardAssignee { class Person(name: String, image: Painter? = null); data object Unassigned }

class MonarchIssueCardLabels(due: ((String) -> String)? = null, overdue: String? = null, tags: ((String) -> String)? = null, unassigned: String? = null, assignee: ((String) -> String)? = null, status: ((String) -> String)? = null, priority: ((String) -> String)? = null, priorityLevel: ((MonarchPriorityLevel) -> String)? = null)

options.name: key
options.description: The issue key, such as STR-142. Shown above the title and read before it.

options.name: status
options.description: The current status, shown with the glyph of its category. Completed and cancelled issues are never overdue.

options.name: statuses
options.description: Every status. With onStatusChange, the status becomes a MonarchStatusPicker.

options.name: priority
options.description: The priority, shown as its glyph at the end of the header. None when null.

options.name: assignee
options.description: Person shows an avatar at the end of the last row; Unassigned an empty dashed slot. No slot when null.

options.name: tags
options.description: Labels on the issue, shown as small MonarchTags.

options.name: dueDate
options.description: The due day in epoch milliseconds, read in UTC as a Material 3 DatePickerState stores it, shown as "Due Mar 12" in the device locale.

options.name: today
options.description: The reference day for overdue, in the same form. The device's current day in its time zone when null.

options.name: selected
options.description: Tints the card with the subtle accent fill and a thicker accent border; the title gets the selected state.

options.name: dragging
options.description: Lifts the card with the large shadow instead of the extra-small one.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the due and overdue text, the priority names and every spoken phrase.

options.name: onStatusChange
options.description: Changes the status from the card. Receives the chosen status id. Needs statuses.

options.name: onPriorityChange
options.description: Changes the priority from the card; the glyph becomes a glyph-only MonarchPriorityPicker.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Opens the issue. Makes the title a button with a 48dp target.

states.name: default
states.description: Surface fill, default border, extra-small shadow.

states.name: selected
states.description: Subtle accent fill and a 2dp accent border instead of the 1dp default one; the title has the selected state.

states.name: dragging
states.description: The large shadow lifts the card.

states.name: overdue
states.description: The due text turns the strong danger color and the word Overdue is added. Completed and cancelled issues are never overdue.

states.name: editable
states.description: Status and priority open Material 3 menus with every option, when their change handlers are given.

appearance: The card uses the MonarchCard surface, large radius and default border. The key is muted caption text and the title strong body text. Priority glyphs use the strong danger, strong warning, default or muted text colors, and status glyphs the subtle, muted, strong warning or strong success colors. The due text is muted, or strong danger when overdue. The same roles adapt to dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Built from MonarchStatusPicker and MonarchPriorityPicker, as the web card uses its StatusPicker and PriorityPicker. MonarchCard has no selected state, so the card draws the same surface with a Material 3 Surface and its own fill and border for selection; the thicker border, not the color alone, marks it. The web's href is not offered: components do not navigate, so the app opens the issue in onOpen. The due date is epoch milliseconds read in UTC (the web also takes YYYY-MM-DD strings and date-times), and today is epoch milliseconds rather than a string. The web's labels are tags here because labels names the strings parameter, as on iOS. The web's calendar glyph is not drawn: Monarch bundles no icons and the word Due carries the meaning. iOS adds a check mark to a selected card; Android marks selection with the thicker border and the selected state. Experimental: a domain pattern until a Rook app adopts it.
accessibility: The title is read with the key first ("STR-142, Sign-in fails…"); with onOpen it is a button with a 48dp touch target, and on a selected card it has the selected state.

A read-only priority is an image read as "Priority: High"; a read-only status is read as "Status: In progress"; the due date as "Due Mar 12, Overdue"; tags as "Labels: Bug, Auth"; the assignee as "Assigned to Ana Ruiz" or "Unassigned".
Editable status and priority are the Monarch pickers: drop-down list role, named with the current value, 48dp touch targets.
Every priority level and status category has its own glyph, overdue is written and selection thickens the border, so nothing relies on color alone.
The title wraps at the largest font scale without being cut.
edgeCases: Long titles wrap; status, tags and the due date flow onto new lines while the assignee stays at the end.
A due date later today is not overdue: days are compared, not times.
With onStatusChange but no statuses, the status stays read-only.
today defaults to the device's current day, so a card shown across midnight changes only when it recomposes; pass today to fix it.

examples.title: Editable status and priority
examples.template:
val configuration = LocalConfiguration.current
val locale = remember(configuration) { Configuration(configuration).apply { setLocale(Locale.US) } }
CompositionLocalProvider(LocalConfiguration provides locale) {
    @OptIn(ExperimentalMonarchApi::class)
    MonarchIssueCard(
        title = {{title}},
        key = {{key}},
        status = statuses.firstOrNull { it.id == statusId },
        statuses = statuses,
        priority = priority,
        assignee = MonarchIssueCardAssignee.Person({{assignee}}),
        tags = listOf({{labels.0}}, {{labels.1}}),
        dueDate = {{dueDate|millis}},
        today = {{today|millis}},
        onStatusChange = { statusId = it },
        onPriorityChange = { priority = it },
        onOpen = { /* Open the issue screen. */ },
    )
}
